# gdk_pixbuf - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gdk_pixbuf/

## Expand description

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rust-gdk-pixbuf-bindings)Rust GDK-PixBuf bindings

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [GDK-Pixbuf](https://docs.gtk.org/gdk-pixbuf), part of [gtk-rs-core](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core).

GDK-PixBuf **2.36.8** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum supported Rust version

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.83.0`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#documentation)Documentation

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#using)Using

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
gdk-pixbuf = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "gdk-pixbuf" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
# This will not compile
[dependencies]
gdk-pixbuf = "0.13"
gdk-pixbuf = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "gdk-pixbuf" }
```
[§](https://gtk-rs.org#see-also)See Also

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#license)License

**gdk-pixbuf** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

- `pub use`- [gio](https://gtk-rs.org/gio/index.html);
- `pub use`- [glib](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/index.html);

# Unlocking the GNOME stack for Rust – gtk-rs

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/

#

          Unlocking the GNOME stack for Rust [§](https://gtk-rs.org#unlocking-the-gnome-stack-for-rust)

The **gtk-rs** project provides safe bindings to the [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org) language for fundamental libraries from the [GNOME](https://developer.gnome.org/components/) stack like [GLib](https://developer.gnome.org/glib), [Cairo](https://cairographics.org/documentation/), and [GTK 4](https://gtk.org).

##

          Available crates [§](https://gtk-rs.org#available-crates)

##

          The introductory book [§](https://gtk-rs.org#the-introductory-book)

  Julian Hofer is writing a book titled [GUI development with Rust and GTK 4](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk4-rs/stable/latest/book). We recommend both new and experienced **gtk-rs** users to have a look at it. While this book is targeted at people who want to develop GTK 4 applications, it also covers more general aspects of the GNOME stack such as **GObject Concepts**, **The Main Event Loop** and **GSettings**.

##

          The gtk-rs ecosystem [§](https://gtk-rs.org#the-gtk-rs-ecosystem)

By now, a number of additional bindings for GObject based libraries exist. While not part of the gtk-rs project, many of them are developed in close collaboration. Notable other projects within the gtk-rs ecosystem are

- **GStreamer**Open source multimedia framework
- **Adwaita**Building blocks for modern GNOME applications
- **SourceView 5**A library extending GtkTextView with features typical for a source code editor
- **Relm 4**An idiomatic GUI library inspired by Elm and based on gtk4-rs

More bindings can be found as part of the [GNOME GitLab Rust Group](https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Rust).

All these bindings are generated on the basis of GObject introspection (GIR). The book [Generate Rust bindings for GIR based libraries](https://gtk-rs.org/gir/book/) provides the documentation for the tools that gtk-rs provides to generate such bindings.

# gio - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gio/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rust-gio-bindings)Rust GIO bindings

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [GIO](https://docs.gtk.org/gio/), part of [gtk-rs-core](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core).

GIO **2.56** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum supported Rust version

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.83.0`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#documentation)Documentation

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#using)Using

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
gio = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "gio" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
# This will not compile
[dependencies]
gio = "0.13"
gio = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "gio" }
```
[§](https://gtk-rs.org#see-also)See Also

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#license)License

**gio** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

- The protocol family of a #GSocketAddress. (These values are
identical to the system defines `AF_INET`,`AF_INET6`and`AF_UNIX`, if available.)
- [Socket](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.SocketListenerEvent.html)- Listener - Event
- Describes an event occurring on a #GSocketListener. See the #GSocketListener::event signal for more details.
- [Socket](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.SocketProtocol.html)- Protocol
- A protocol identifier is specified when creating a #GSocket, which is a family/type specific identifier, where 0 means the default protocol for the particular family/type.
- [Socket](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.SocketType.html)- Type
- Flags used when creating a #GSocket. Some protocols may not implement all the socket types.
- [TlsAuthentication](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TlsAuthenticationMode.html)- Mode
- The client authentication mode for a #GTlsServerConnection.
- [TlsChannel](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TlsChannelBindingError.html)- Binding - Error - `v2_66`
- An error code used with `G_TLS_CHANNEL_BINDING_ERROR`in a #GError to indicate a TLS channel binding retrieval error.
- [TlsChannel](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TlsChannelBindingType.html)- Binding - Type - `v2_66`
- The type of TLS channel binding data to retrieve from #GTlsConnection
or #GDtlsConnection, as documented by RFC 5929 or RFC 9266. The
`tls-unique-for-telnet`
- [TlsError](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TlsError.html)
- An error code used with `G_TLS_ERROR`in a #GError returned from a TLS-related routine.
- [TlsInteraction](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TlsInteractionResult.html)- Result
- #GTlsInteractionResult is returned by various functions in #GTlsInteraction when finishing an interaction request.
- [TlsProtocol](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TlsProtocolVersion.html)- Version - `v2_70`
- The TLS or DTLS protocol version used by a #GTlsConnection or
#GDtlsConnection. The integer values of these versions are sequential
to ensure newer known protocol versions compare greater than older
known versions. Any known DTLS protocol version will compare greater
than any SSL or TLS protocol version. The protocol version may be
`Unknown`
- [TlsRehandshake](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TlsRehandshakeMode.html)- Mode - Deprecated
- When to allow rehandshaking. See g_tls_connection_set_rehandshake_mode().
- [Unix](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.UnixSocketAddressType.html)- Socket - Address - Type - Unix
- The type of name used by a #GUnixSocketAddress.
`Path``Anonymous`
- [Zlib](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.ZlibCompressorFormat.html)- Compressor - Format
- Used to select the type of data format to use for #GZlibDecompressor and #GZlibCompressor.

## Functions[§](https://gtk-rs.org#functions)

- [bus_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.bus_own_name.html)- own_ - name
- Requests ownership of @name on the bus specified by @bus_type.
- [bus_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.bus_own_name_on_connection.html)- own_ - name_ - on_ - connection
- Like `bus_own_name()`but takes a`DBusConnection``BusType`
- [bus_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.bus_unown_name.html)- unown_ - name
- [bus_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.bus_unwatch_name.html)- unwatch_ - name
- [bus_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.bus_watch_name.html)- watch_ - name
- Starts watching @name on the bus specified by @bus_type and calls
@name_appeared_handler and @name_vanished_handler when the name is
known to have an owner respectively known to lose its
owner. Callbacks will be invoked in the thread-default main context
(see [`glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()`][crate::glib::MainContext::push_thread_default()]) of the thread you are calling this function from.
- [bus_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.bus_watch_name_on_connection.html)- watch_ - name_ - on_ - connection
- Like g_bus_watch_name() but takes a #GDBusConnection instead of a #GBusType.
- [spawn_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.spawn_blocking.html)- blocking
- Runs a blocking I/O task on the I/O thread pool.

# glib - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rust-glib-and-gobject-bindings)Rust GLib and GObject bindings

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [GLib](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/), part of [gtk-rs-core](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core).

GLib **2.56** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

This library contains bindings to GLib and GObject types and APIs as well as common building blocks used in both handmade and machine generated bindings to GTK and other GLib-based libraries.

It is the foundation for higher level libraries with uniform Rusty (safe and strongly typed) APIs. It avoids exposing GLib-specific data types where possible and is not meant to provide comprehensive GLib bindings, which would often amount to duplicating the Rust Standard Library or other utility crates.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum supported Rust version

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.83.0`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dynamic-typing)Dynamic typing

Most types in the GLib family have [ Type](https://gtk-rs.org/types/struct.Type.html) identifiers.
Their corresponding Rust types implement the

[trait.](https://gtk-rs.org/types/trait.StaticType.html)

`StaticType`A dynamically typed [ Value](https://gtk-rs.org/value/struct.Value.html) can carry values of any

`StaticType`.
[Variants](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/variant/struct.Variant.html)can carry values of

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/variant/trait.StaticVariantType.html)

`StaticVariantType`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#errors)Errors

Errors are represented by [ Error](https://gtk-rs.org/error/struct.Error.html), which can
carry values from various

[error domains](https://gtk-rs.org/error/trait.ErrorDomain.html)such as

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileError.html)

`FileError`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#objects)Objects

Each class and interface has a corresponding smart pointer struct
representing an instance of that type (e.g. [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html) for

[or](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/class.Object.html)

`GObject`[for](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk4-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk4/struct.Widget.html)

`gtk4::Widget`[). They are reference counted and feature interior mutability similarly to Rust’s](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Widget.html)

`GtkWidget`[idiom. Consequently, cloning objects is cheap and their methods never require mutable borrows. Two smart pointers are equal if they point to the same object.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cell/index.html#introducing-mutability-inside-of-something-immutable)

`Rc<RefCell<T>>`The root of the object hierarchy is [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html).
Inheritance and subtyping is denoted with the

[marker trait. The](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.IsA.html)

`IsA`[trait enables upcasting and downcasting.](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.Cast.html)

`Cast`Interfaces and non-leaf classes also have corresponding traits (e.g.
[ ObjectExt](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.ObjectExt.html) or

[), which are blanketly implemented for all their subtypes.](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk4-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk4/prelude/trait.WidgetExt.html)

`WidgetExt`You can create new subclasses of [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html) or other object types. Look at
the module’s documentation for further details and a code example.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#under-the-hood)Under the hood

GLib-based libraries largely operate on pointers to various boxed or
reference counted structures so the bindings have to implement corresponding
smart pointers (wrappers), which encapsulate resource management and safety
checks. Such wrappers are defined via the
[ wrapper!](https://gtk-rs.org/macro.wrapper.html) macro, which uses abstractions
defined in the

[,](https://gtk-rs.org/wrapper/index.html)

`wrapper`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/boxed/index.html)

`boxed`[and](https://gtk-rs.org/shared/index.html)

`shared`[modules. The](https://gtk-rs.org/object/index.html)

`object`[module defines and partly implements conversions between high level Rust types (including the aforementioned wrappers) and their FFI counterparts.](https://gtk-rs.org/translate/index.html)

`translate`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#documentation)Documentation

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#using)Using

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
glib = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "glib" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
# This will not compile
[dependencies]
glib = "0.13"
glib = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "glib" }
```
[§](https://gtk-rs.org#license)License

**glib** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

- [File](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileError.html)- Error
- Values corresponding to @errno codes returned from file operations on UNIX. Unlike @errno codes, GFileError values are available on all systems, even Windows. The exact meaning of each code depends on what sort of file operation you were performing; the UNIX documentation gives more details. The following error code descriptions come from the GNU C Library manual, and are under the copyright of that manual.

- The #GOptionArg enum values determine which type of extra argument the

- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_ONLY_SHOW_IN.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - ONLY_ - SHOW_ - IN
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a list of strings identifying the environments that should display the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_PATH.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - PATH
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string containing the working directory to run the program in.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_STARTUP_NOTIFY.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - STARTUP_ - NOTIFY
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a boolean stating whether the application supports the[Startup Notification Protocol Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/startup-notification-spec/latest/).
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_STARTUP_WM_CLASS.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - STARTUP_ - WM_ - CLASS
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is string identifying the WM class or name hint of a window that the application will create, which can be used to emulate[Startup Notification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/startup-notification-spec/latest/)with older applications.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TERMINAL.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - TERMINAL
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a boolean stating whether the program should be run in a terminal window.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TRY_EXEC.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - TRY_ - EXEC
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the file name of a binary on disk used to determine if the program is actually installed.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - TYPE
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the type of the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_URL.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - URL
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the URL to access.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_VERSION.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - VERSION
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the version of the Desktop Entry Specification used for the desktop entry file.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_TYPE_APPLICATION.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - TYPE_ - APPLICATION
- The value of the `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE`, key for desktop entries representing applications.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_TYPE_DIRECTORY.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - TYPE_ - DIRECTORY
- The value of the `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE`, key for desktop entries representing directories.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_TYPE_LINK.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - TYPE_ - LINK
- The value of the `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE`, key for desktop entries representing links to documents.
- [OPTION_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.OPTION_REMAINING.html)- REMAINING
- If a long option in the main group has this name, it is not treated as a
regular option. Instead it collects all non-option arguments which would
otherwise be left in `argv`. The option must be of type`OptionArg::Callback``OptionArg::StringArray``OptionArg::FilenameArray`
- [STR_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.STR_DELIMITERS.html)- DELIMITERS
- The standard delimiters, used in `strdelimit()`.
- [TEST_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.TEST_OPTION_ISOLATE_DIRS.html)- OPTION_ - ISOLATE_ - DIRS - `v2_60`
- A value that can be passed as an option to `test_init()`.
- [TEST_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.TEST_OPTION_NONFATAL_ASSERTIONS.html)- OPTION_ - NONFATAL_ - ASSERTIONS - `v2_84`
- A value that can be passed as an option to `test_init()`.
- [TEST_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.TEST_OPTION_NO_PRGNAME.html)- OPTION_ - NO_ - PRGNAME - `v2_84`
- A value that can be passed as an option to `test_init()`.
- [URI_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.URI_RESERVED_CHARS_GENERIC_DELIMITERS.html)- RESERVED_ - CHARS_ - GENERIC_ - DELIMITERS
- Generic delimiters characters as defined in
[RFC 3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986). Includes`:/?#[]@`.
- [URI_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.URI_RESERVED_CHARS_SUBCOMPONENT_DELIMITERS.html)- RESERVED_ - CHARS_ - SUBCOMPONENT_ - DELIMITERS
- Subcomponent delimiter characters as defined in
[RFC 3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986). Includes`!$&'()*+,;=`.

## Functions[§](https://gtk-rs.org#functions)

- [access](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.access.html)
- A wrapper for the POSIX access() function. This function is used to test a pathname for one or several of read, write or execute permissions, or just existence.
- [application_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.application_name.html)- name
- Gets a human-readable name for the application, as set by
g_set_application_name(). This name should be localized if
possible, and is intended for display to the user.  Contrast with
g_get_prgname(), which gets a non-localized name. If
g_set_application_name() has not been called, returns the result of
g_get_prgname() (which may be `None`
- [base64_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.base64_decode.html)- decode
- Decode a sequence of Base-64 encoded text into binary data. Note that the returned binary data is not necessarily zero-terminated, so it should not be used as a character string.
- [base64_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.base64_encode.html)- encode
- Encode a sequence of binary data into its Base-64 stringified representation.
- [casefold](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.casefold.html)

- [compute_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.compute_checksum_for_data.html)- checksum_ - for_ - data
- Computes the checksum for a binary @data of @length. This is a convenience wrapper for g_checksum_new(), g_checksum_get_string() and g_checksum_free().

- [convert](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.convert.html)
- Converts a string from one character set to another.
- [convert_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.convert_with_fallback.html)- with_ - fallback
- Converts a string from one character set to another, possibly including fallback sequences for characters not representable in the output. Note that it is not guaranteed that the specification for the fallback sequences in @fallback will be honored. Some systems may do an approximate conversion from @from_codeset to @to_codeset in their iconv() functions, in which case GLib will simply return that approximate conversion.
- [current_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.current_dir.html)- dir
- Gets the current directory.
- [dcgettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dcgettext.html)
- This is a variant of g_dgettext() that allows specifying a locale
category instead of always using `LC_MESSAGES`. See g_dgettext() for more information about how this functions differs from calling dcgettext() directly.
- [dgettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dgettext.html)
- This function is a wrapper of dgettext() which does not translate the message if the default domain as set with textdomain() has no translations for the current locale.
- [dngettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dngettext.html)
- This function is a wrapper of dngettext() which does not translate the message if the default domain as set with textdomain() has no translations for the current locale.
- [dpgettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dpgettext.html)
- This function is a variant of g_dgettext() which supports a disambiguating message context. GNU gettext uses the ‘\004’ character to separate the message context and message id in @msgctxtid. If 0 is passed as @msgidoffset, this function will fall back to trying to use the deprecated convention of using “|” as a separation character.
- [dpgettext2](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dpgettext2.html)
- This function is a variant of g_dgettext() which supports a disambiguating message context. GNU gettext uses the ‘\004’ character to separate the message context and message id in @msgctxtid.
- [environ](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.environ.html)
- Gets the list of environment variables for the current process.
- [environ_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.environ_getenv.html)- getenv
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_get_contents.html)- get_ - contents
- Reads an entire file into allocated memory, with good error checking.
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_open_tmp.html)- open_ - tmp - Unix
- Opens a file for writing in the preferred directory for temporary files (as returned by g_get_tmp_dir()).
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_set_contents.html)- set_ - contents
- Writes all of @contents to a file named @filename. This is a convenience
wrapper around calling g_file_set_contents_full() with `flags`set to`G_FILE_SET_CONTENTS_CONSISTENT | G_FILE_SET_CONTENTS_ONLY_EXISTING`and`mode`set to`0666`.
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_set_contents_full.html)- set_ - contents_ - full - `v2_66`
- Writes all of @contents to a file named @filename, with good error checking. If a file called @filename already exists it will be overwritten.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_charsets.html)- charsets
- Determines the preferred character sets used for filenames. The first character set from the @charsets is the filename encoding, the subsequent character sets are used when trying to generate a displayable representation of a filename, see g_filename_display_name().
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_display_basename.html)- display_ - basename
- Returns the display basename for the particular filename, guaranteed to be valid UTF-8. The display name might not be identical to the filename, for instance there might be problems converting it to UTF-8, and some files can be translated in the display.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_display_name.html)- display_ - name
- Converts a filename into a valid UTF-8 string. The conversion is
not necessarily reversible, so you should keep the original around
and use the return value of this function only for display purposes.
Unlike g_filename_to_utf8(), the result is guaranteed to be non-`None`
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_from_uri.html)- from_ - uri
- Converts an escaped ASCII-encoded URI to a local filename in the encoding used for filenames.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_from_utf8.html)- from_ - utf8
- Converts a string from UTF-8 to the encoding GLib uses for
filenames. Note that on Windows GLib uses UTF-8 for filenames;
on other platforms, this function indirectly depends on the
[current locale](https://gtk-rs.org/running.html#locale).
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_to_uri.html)- to_ - uri
- Converts an absolute filename to an escaped ASCII-encoded URI, with the path component following Section 3.3. of RFC 2396.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_to_utf8.html)- to_ - utf8
- Converts a string which is in the encoding used by GLib for
filenames into a UTF-8 string. Note that on Windows GLib uses UTF-8
for filenames; on other platforms, this function indirectly depends on
the [current locale](https://gtk-rs.org/running.html#locale).
- [find_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.find_program_in_path.html)- program_ - in_ - path
- Locates the first executable named @program in the user’s path, in the
same way that execvp() would locate it. Returns an allocated string
with the absolute path name, or `None``None`
- [format_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.format_size.html)- size
- Formats a size (for example the size of a file) into a human readable string. Sizes are rounded to the nearest size prefix (kB, MB, GB) and are displayed rounded to the nearest tenth. E.g. the file size 3292528 bytes will be converted into the string “3.2 MB”. The returned string is UTF-8, and may use a non-breaking space to separate the number and units, to ensure they aren’t separated when line wrapped.
- [format_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.format_size_full.html)- size_ - full
- Formats a size.

- [hostname_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.hostname_to_unicode.html)- to_ - unicode

# Pixbuf in gdk_pixbuf - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gdk_pixbuf/struct.Pixbuf.html

`pub struct Pixbuf { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A pixel buffer.

[ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html) contains information about an image’s pixel data,
its color space, bits per sample, width and height, and the
rowstride (the number of bytes between the start of one row
and the start of the next).

The most basic way to create a pixbuf is to wrap an existing pixel
buffer with a [class[ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)] instance. You can use the
[

`ctor[`Pixbuf`][crate::Pixbuf].new_from_data`] function to do this.Every time you create a new [ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html) instance for some data, you
will need to specify the destroy notification function that will be
called when the data buffer needs to be freed; this will happen when
a

[is finalized by the reference counting functions. If you have a chunk of static data compiled into your application, you can pass in](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)

`Pixbuf``NULL` as the destroy notification function so that the
data will not be freed.The [`ctor[`Pixbuf`][crate::Pixbuf].new`] constructor function can be used
as a convenience to create a pixbuf with an empty buffer; this is
equivalent to allocating a data buffer using `malloc()` and then
wrapping it with `gdk_pixbuf_new_from_data()`. The `[`new()`][Self::new()]`
function will compute an optimal rowstride so that rendering can be
performed with an efficient algorithm.

You can also copy an existing pixbuf with the [method`Pixbuf`]
function. This is not the same as just acquiring a reference to
the old pixbuf instance: the copy function will actually duplicate
the pixel data in memory and create a new [class`Pixbuf`] instance
for it.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#reference-counting)Reference counting

[ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html) structures are reference counted. This means that an
application can share a single pixbuf among many parts of the
code. When a piece of the program needs to use a pixbuf, it should
acquire a reference to it by calling

`g_object_ref()`; when it no
longer needs the pixbuf, it should release the reference it acquired
by calling `g_object_unref()`. The resources associated with a
[will be freed when its reference count drops to zero. Newly-created](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)

`Pixbuf`[instances start with a reference count of one.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)

`Pixbuf`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#image-data)Image Data

Image data in a pixbuf is stored in memory in an uncompressed, packed format. Rows in the image are stored top to bottom, and in each row pixels are stored from left to right.

There may be padding at the end of a row.

The “rowstride” value of a pixbuf, as returned by [`method[`Pixbuf`][crate::Pixbuf].get_rowstride`],
indicates the number of bytes between rows.

**NOTE**: If you are copying raw pixbuf data with `memcpy()` note that the
last row in the pixbuf may not be as wide as the full rowstride, but rather
just as wide as the pixel data needs to be; that is: it is unsafe to do
`memcpy (dest, pixels, rowstride * height)` to copy a whole pixbuf. Use
[method[ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html).copy] instead, or compute the width in bytes of the
last row as:

**⚠️ The following code is in c ⚠️**

`last_row = width * ((n_channels * bits_per_sample + 7) / 8);`The same rule applies when iterating over each row of a [ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html) pixels
array.

The following code illustrates a simple `put_pixel()`
function for RGB pixbufs with 8 bits per channel with an alpha
channel.

**⚠️ The following code is in c ⚠️**

```
static void
put_pixel (GdkPixbuf *pixbuf,
           int x,
       int y,
       guchar red,
       guchar green,
       guchar blue,
       guchar alpha)
{
  int n_channels = gdk_pixbuf_get_n_channels (pixbuf);
  // Ensure that the pixbuf is valid
  g_assert (gdk_pixbuf_get_colorspace (pixbuf) == GDK_COLORSPACE_RGB);
  g_assert (gdk_pixbuf_get_bits_per_sample (pixbuf) == 8);
  g_assert (gdk_pixbuf_get_has_alpha (pixbuf));
  g_assert (n_channels == 4);
  int width = gdk_pixbuf_get_width (pixbuf);
  int height = gdk_pixbuf_get_height (pixbuf);
  // Ensure that the coordinates are in a valid range
  g_assert (x >= 0 && x < width);
  g_assert (y >= 0 && y < height);
  int rowstride = gdk_pixbuf_get_rowstride (pixbuf);
  // The pixel buffer in the GdkPixbuf instance
  guchar *pixels = gdk_pixbuf_get_pixels (pixbuf);
  // The pixel we wish to modify
  guchar *p = pixels + y * rowstride + x * n_channels;
  p[0] = red;
  p[1] = green;
  p[2] = blue;
  p[3] = alpha;
}
```
[§](https://gtk-rs.org#loading-images)Loading images

The `GdkPixBuf` class provides a simple mechanism for loading
an image from a file in synchronous and asynchronous fashion.

For GUI applications, it is recommended to use the asynchronous stream API to avoid blocking the control flow of the application.

Additionally, [ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html) provides the [class

[`] API for progressive image loading.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)

`Pixbuf`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#saving-images)Saving images

The [ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html) class provides methods for saving image data in
a number of file formats. The formatted data can be written to a
file or to a memory buffer.

[can also call a user-defined callback on the data, which allows to e.g. write the image to a socket or store it in a database.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-1)Returns

A newly-created pixbuf

Creates a new pixbuf by loading an image from a file.

The file format is detected automatically.

If `NULL` is returned, then `error` will be set. Possible errors are:

- the file could not be opened
- there is no loader for the file’s format
- there is not enough memory to allocate the image buffer
- the image buffer contains invalid data

The error domains are `GDK_PIXBUF_ERROR` and `G_FILE_ERROR`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#filename)`filename`

Name of file to load, in the GLib file name encoding

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/auto/pixbuf.rs.html#386-407)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/auto/pixbuf.rs.html#386-407)

Creates a new pixbuf by loading an image from a file.

The file format is detected automatically.

If `NULL` is returned, then `error` will be set. Possible errors are:

- the file could not be opened
- there is no loader for the file’s format
- there is not enough memory to allocate the image buffer
- the image buffer contains invalid data

The error domains are `GDK_PIXBUF_ERROR` and `G_FILE_ERROR`.

The image will be scaled to fit in the requested size, optionally preserving the image’s aspect ratio.

When preserving the aspect ratio, a `width` of -1 will cause the image
to be scaled to the exact given height, and a `height` of -1 will cause
the image to be scaled to the exact given width. When not preserving
aspect ratio, a `width` or `height` of -1 means to not scale the image
at all in that dimension. Negative values for `width` and `height` are
allowed since 2.8.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#filename-1)`filename`

Name of file to load, in the GLib file name encoding

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#width-3)`width`

The width the image should have or -1 to not constrain the width

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#height-3)`height`

The height the image should have or -1 to not constrain the height

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#preserve_aspect_ratio)`preserve_aspect_ratio`

`TRUE` to preserve the image’s aspect ratio

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/auto/pixbuf.rs.html#440-459)

Creates a new pixbuf by loading an image from a file.

The file format is detected automatically.

If `NULL` is returned, then `error` will be set. Possible errors are:

- the file could not be opened
- there is no loader for the file’s format
- there is not enough memory to allocate the image buffer
- the image buffer contains invalid data

The error domains are `GDK_PIXBUF_ERROR` and `G_FILE_ERROR`.

The image will be scaled to fit in the requested size, preserving
the image’s aspect ratio. Note that the returned pixbuf may be smaller
than `width` x `height`, if the aspect ratio requires it. To load
and image at the requested size, regardless of aspect ratio, use
[ctor[ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html).new_from_file_at_scale].

from another thread. If the operation was cancelled, the error
`G_IO_ERROR_CANCELLED` will be returned. Other possible errors are in
the `GDK_PIXBUF_ERROR` and `G_IO_ERROR` domains.

The image will be scaled to fit in the requested size, optionally preserving the image’s aspect ratio.

When preserving the aspect ratio, a `width` of -1 will cause the image to be
scaled to the exact given height, and a `height` of -1 will cause the image
to be scaled to the exact given width. If both `width` and `height` are
given, this function will behave as if the smaller of the two values
is passed as -1.

When not preserving aspect ratio, a `width` or `height` of -1 means to not
scale the image at all in that dimension.

The stream is not closed.

Takes an existing pixbuf and adds an alpha channel to it.

If the existing pixbuf already had an alpha channel, the channel values are copied from the original; otherwise, the alpha channel is initialized to 255 (full opacity).

If `substitute_color` is `TRUE`, then the color specified by the
(`r`, `g`, `b`) arguments will be assigned zero opacity. That is,
if you pass `(255, 255, 255)` for the substitute color, all white
pixels will become fully transparent.

If `substitute_color` is `FALSE`, then the (`r`, `g`, `b`) arguments
will be ignored.

Takes an existing pixbuf and checks for the presence of an associated “orientation” option.

The orientation option may be provided by the JPEG loader (which reads the exif orientation tag) or the TIFF loader (which reads the TIFF orientation tag, and compensates it for the partial transforms performed by libtiff).

If an orientation option/tag is present, the appropriate transform will be performed so that the pixbuf is oriented correctly.

Creates a transformation of the source image `self` by scaling by
`scale_x` and `scale_y` then translating by `offset_x` and `offset_y`.

This gives an image in the coordinates of the destination pixbuf.
The rectangle (`dest_x`, `dest_y`, `dest_width`, `dest_height`)
is then alpha blended onto the corresponding rectangle of the
original destination image.

When the destination rectangle contains parts not in the source image, the data at the edges of the source image is replicated to infinity.

Creates a transformation of the source image `self` by scaling by
`scale_x` and `scale_y` then translating by `offset_x` and `offset_y`,
then alpha blends the rectangle (`dest_x` ,`dest_y`, `dest_width`,
`dest_height`) of the resulting image with a checkboard of the
colors `color1` and `color2` and renders it onto the destination
image.

If the source image has no alpha channel, and `overall_alpha` is 255, a fast
path is used which omits the alpha blending and just performs the scaling.

function suitable for many tasks.

Looks up `key` in the list of options that may have been attached to the
`self` when it was loaded, or that may have been attached by another
function using [ set_option()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html#method.set_option).

For instance, the ANI loader provides “Title” and “Artist” options. The ICO, XBM, and XPM loaders provide “x_hot” and “y_hot” hot-spot options for cursor definitions. The PNG loader provides the tEXt ancillary chunk key/value pairs as options. Since 2.12, the TIFF and JPEG loaders return an “orientation” option string that corresponds to the embedded TIFF/Exif orientation tag (if present). Since 2.32, the TIFF loader sets the “multipage” option string to “yes” when a multi-page TIFF is loaded. Since 2.32 the JPEG and PNG loaders set “x-dpi” and “y-dpi” if the file contains image density information in dots per inch. Since 2.36.6, the JPEG loader sets the “comment” option with the comment EXIF tag.

a nul-terminated string.

Creates a new pixbuf which represents a sub-region of `src_pixbuf`.

The new pixbuf shares its pixels with the original pixbuf, so
writing to one affects both. The new pixbuf holds a reference to
`src_pixbuf`, so `src_pixbuf` will not be finalized until the new
pixbuf is finalized.

Note that if `src_pixbuf` is read-only, this function will force it
to be mutable.

Modifies saturation and optionally pixelates `src`, placing the result in
`dest`.

The `src` and `dest` pixbufs must have the same image format, size, and
rowstride.

The `src` and `dest` arguments may be the same pixbuf with no ill effects.

If `saturation` is 1.0 then saturation is not changed. If it’s less than 1.0,
saturation is reduced (the image turns toward grayscale); if greater than
1.0, saturation is increased (the image gets more vivid colors).

If `pixelate` is `TRUE`, then pixels are faded in a checkerboard pattern to
create a pixelated image.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dest-2)`dest`

place to write modified version of `self`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#saturation)`saturation`

saturation factor

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#pixelate)`pixelate`

whether to pixelate

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/auto/pixbuf.rs.html#1360-1388)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/auto/pixbuf.rs.html#1360-1388)

Creates a transformation of the source image `self` by scaling by
`scale_x` and `scale_y` then translating by `offset_x` and `offset_y`,
then renders the rectangle (`dest_x`, `dest_y`, `dest_width`,
`dest_height`) of the resulting image onto the destination image
replacing the previous contents.

Try to use [ scale_simple()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html#method.scale_simple) first; this function is
the industrial-strength power tool you can fall back to, if

[isn’t powerful enough.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html#method.scale_simple)

`scale_simple()`If the source rectangle overlaps the destination rectangle on the same pixbuf, it will be overwritten during the scaling which results in rendering artifacts.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dest_y-3)`dest_y`

the top coordinate for region to render

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dest_width-3)`dest_width`

the width of the region to render

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dest_height-3)`dest_height`

the height of the region to render

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#offset_x-2)`offset_x`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#offset_y-2)`offset_y`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#scale_y-2)`scale_y`

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/auto/pixbuf.rs.html#1420-1434)#### pub fn [scale_simple](https://gtk-rs.org#method.scale_simple)(

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/auto/pixbuf.rs.html#1420-1434)

#### pub fn [scale_simple](https://gtk-rs.org#method.scale_simple)(
    &self,
    dest_width: [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html),
    dest_height: [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html),
    interp_type: [InterpType](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.InterpType.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)>

Create a new pixbuf containing a copy of `src` scaled to
`dest_width` x `dest_height`.

This function leaves `src` unaffected.

The `interp_type` should be `GDK_INTERP_NEAREST` if you want maximum
speed (but when scaling down `GDK_INTERP_NEAREST` is usually unusably
ugly). The default `interp_type` should be `GDK_INTERP_BILINEAR` which
offers reasonable quality and speed.

You can scale a sub-portion of `src` by creating a sub-pixbuf
pointing into `src`; see [method[ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html).new_subpixbuf].

If `dest_width` and `dest_height` are equal to the width and height of
`src`, this function will return an unscaled copy of `src`.

For more complicated scaling/alpha blending see [method[ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html).scale]
and [method

[.composite].](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)

`Pixbuf`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dest_width-4)`dest_width`

the width of destination image

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dest_height-4)`dest_height`

the height of destination image

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#interp_type-4)`interp_type`

the interpolation type for the transformation.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-28)Returns

the new pixbuf

Initalizes the gdk-pixbuf loader modules referenced by the `loaders.cache`
file present inside that directory.

This is to be used by applications that want to ship certain loaders in a different location from the system ones.

This is needed when the OS or runtime ships a minimal number of loaders so as to reduce the potential attack surface of carefully crafted image files, especially for uncommon file types. Applications that require broader image file types coverage, such as image viewers, would be expected to ship the gdk-pixbuf modules in a separate location, bundled with the application in a separate directory from the OS or runtime- provided modules.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#path)`path`

Path to directory where the `loaders.cache` is installed

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#cancellable-4)`cancellable`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#callback-1)`callback`

a `GAsyncReadyCallback` to call when the pixbuf is saved

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/pixbuf.rs.html#604-632)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/pixbuf.rs.html#654-678)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/pixbuf.rs.html#654-678)

Vector version of `gdk_pixbuf_save()`.

Saves pixbuf to a file in `type`, which is currently “jpeg”, “png”, “tiff”, “ico” or “bmp”.

If `error` is set, `FALSE` will be returned.

See [method[ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html).save] for more details.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#filename-5)`filename`

name of file to save.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#type_-3)`type_`

name of file format.

name of options to set

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#option_values-3)`option_values`

values for named options

whether an error was set

and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will

# PixbufAnimation in gdk_pixbuf - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gdk_pixbuf/struct.PixbufAnimation.html

`pub struct PixbufAnimation { /* private fields */ }`Since 2.44

## Expand description

Use a different image loading library for animatable assets An opaque object representing an animation.

The GdkPixBuf library provides a simple mechanism to load and represent animations. An animation is conceptually a series of frames to be displayed over time.

The animation may not be represented as a series of frames internally; for example, it may be stored as a sprite and instructions for moving the sprite around a background.

To display an animation you don’t need to understand its
representation, however; you just ask [ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html) what should
be displayed at a given point in time.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

[ PixbufAnimationExt](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PixbufAnimationExt.html),

`PixbufAnimationExtManual`GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

Since 2.44

Creates a new animation by loading it from an input stream.

The file format is detected automatically.

If `NULL` is returned, then `error` will be set.

The `cancellable` can be used to abort the operation from another thread.
If the operation was cancelled, the error `G_IO_ERROR_CANCELLED` will be
returned. Other possible errors are in the `GDK_PIXBUF_ERROR` and
`G_IO_ERROR` domains.

The stream is not closed.

Creates a new animation by asynchronously loading an image from an input stream.

For more details see [ Pixbuf::from_stream()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html#method.from_stream), which is the synchronous
version of this function.

When the operation is finished, `callback` will be called in the main thread.
You can then call `gdk_pixbuf_animation_new_from_stream_finish()` to get the
result of the operation.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#method.dynamic_cast)

#### fn [dynamic_cast](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)<T>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, Self>

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

# PixbufAnimationIter in gdk_pixbuf - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gdk_pixbuf/struct.PixbufAnimationIter.html

`pub struct PixbufAnimationIter { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Use a different image loading library for animatable assets An opaque object representing an iterator which points to a certain position in an animation.

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/pixbuf_animation_iter.rs.html#54-68)#### pub fn [advance](https://gtk-rs.org#method.advance)(&self, current_time: [SystemTime](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/time/struct.SystemTime.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/pixbuf_animation_iter.rs.html#54-68)

#### pub fn [advance](https://gtk-rs.org#method.advance)(&self, current_time: [SystemTime](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/time/struct.SystemTime.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Possibly advances an animation to a new frame.

Chooses the frame based on the start time passed to
[ PixbufAnimationExtManual::iter()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PixbufAnimationExtManual.html#method.iter).

`current_time` would normally come from `g_get_current_time()`, and
must be greater than or equal to the time passed to
[ PixbufAnimationExtManual::iter()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PixbufAnimationExtManual.html#method.iter), and must increase or remain
unchanged each time [

`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::pixbuf()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::pixbuf()] is
called. That is, you can’t go backward in time; animations only
play forward.As a shortcut, pass `NULL` for the current time and `g_get_current_time()`
will be invoked on your behalf. So you only need to explicitly pass
`current_time` if you’re doing something odd like playing the animation
at double speed.

If this function returns `FALSE`, there’s no need to update the animation
display, assuming the display had been rendered prior to advancing;
if `TRUE`, you need to call [`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::pixbuf()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::pixbuf()]
and update the display with the new pixbuf.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#deprecated-since-244)Deprecated since 2.44

Use a different image loading library for animatable assets

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#current_time)`current_time`

current time

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns)Returns

`TRUE` if the image may need updating

Gets the current pixbuf which should be displayed.

The pixbuf might not be the same size as the animation itself
([ PixbufAnimationExt::width()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PixbufAnimationExt.html#method.width),

[).](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PixbufAnimationExt.html#method.height)

`PixbufAnimationExt::height()`This pixbuf should be displayed for [`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::delay_time()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::delay_time()]
milliseconds.

The caller of this function does not own a reference to the returned
pixbuf; the returned pixbuf will become invalid when the iterator
advances to the next frame, which may happen anytime you call
[`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::advance()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::advance()].

Copy the pixbuf to keep it (don’t just add a reference), as it may get recycled as you advance the iterator.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#deprecated-since-244-1)Deprecated since 2.44

Use a different image loading library for animatable assets

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-1)Returns

the pixbuf to be displayed

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/pixbuf_animation_iter.rs.html#122-132)#### pub fn [delay_time](https://gtk-rs.org#method.delay_time)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/pixbuf_animation_iter.rs.html#122-132)

#### pub fn [delay_time](https://gtk-rs.org#method.delay_time)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>

Gets the number of milliseconds the current pixbuf should be displayed, or -1 if the current pixbuf should be displayed forever.

The `g_timeout_add()` function conveniently takes a timeout in milliseconds,
so you can use a timeout to schedule the next update.

Note that some formats, like GIF, might clamp the timeout values in the image file to avoid updates that are just too quick. The minimum timeout for GIF images is currently 20 milliseconds.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#deprecated-since-244-2)Deprecated since 2.44

Use a different image loading library for animatable assets

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-2)Returns

delay time in milliseconds (thousandths of a second)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/pixbuf_animation_iter.rs.html#149-155)#### pub fn [on_currently_loading_frame](https://gtk-rs.org#method.on_currently_loading_frame)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/pixbuf_animation_iter.rs.html#149-155)

#### pub fn [on_currently_loading_frame](https://gtk-rs.org#method.on_currently_loading_frame)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Used to determine how to respond to the area_updated signal on
[ PixbufLoader](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PixbufLoader.html) when loading an animation.

The `::area_updated` signal is emitted for an area of the frame currently
streaming in to the loader. So if you’re on the currently loading frame,
you will need to redraw the screen for the updated area.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#deprecated-since-244-3)Deprecated since 2.44

Use a different image loading library for animatable assets

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-3)Returns

`TRUE` if the frame we’re on is partially loaded, or the last frame

# PixbufFormat in gdk_pixbuf - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gdk_pixbuf/struct.PixbufFormat.html

`pub struct PixbufFormat { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ PixbufFormat](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PixbufFormat.html) contains information about the image format accepted
by a module.

Only modules should access the fields directly, applications should
use the `gdk_pixbuf_format_*` family of functions.

GLib type: Boxed type with copy-on-clone semantics.

#### fn [sub_assign](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/arith/trait.SubAssign.html#tymethod.sub_assign)(&mut self, other: Self)

The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).

This method is not equivalent to `self & !other` when `other` has unknown bits set.
`difference` won’t truncate `other`, but the `!` operator will.

# PixbufLoader in gdk_pixbuf - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gdk_pixbuf/struct.PixbufLoader.html

`pub struct PixbufLoader { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Incremental image loader.

[ PixbufLoader](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PixbufLoader.html) provides a way for applications to drive the
process of loading an image, by letting them send the image data
directly to the loader instead of having the loader read the data
from a file. Applications can use this functionality instead of

`[`Pixbuf::from_file()`][crate::Pixbuf::from_file()]` or `[`PixbufAnimation::from_file()`][crate::PixbufAnimation::from_file()]`
when they need to parse image data in small chunks. For example,
it should be used when reading an image from a (potentially) slow
network connection, or when loading an extremely large file.To use [ PixbufLoader](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PixbufLoader.html) to load an image, create a new instance,
and call [method

[.write] to send the data to it. When done, [method](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)

`Pixbuf`[.close] should be called to end the stream and finalize everything.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)

`Pixbuf`The loader will emit three important signals throughout the process:

- [signal`Pixbuf``Pixbuf`
- [signal`Pixbuf``Pixbuf``Pixbuf``[`PixbufLoaderExt::pixbuf()`][crate::prelude::PixbufLoaderExt::pixbuf()]`later to get the same pixbuf.
- [signal`Pixbuf`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#loading-an-animation)Loading an animation

Loading an animation is almost as easy as loading an image. Once the
first [signal[ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)::area-prepared] signal has been
emitted, you can call [method

[.get_animation] to get the [class](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)

`Pixbuf`[] instance, and then call and [method](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)

`Pixbuf`[.get_iter] to get a [class](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)

`Pixbuf`[] to retrieve the pixbuf for the desired time stamp.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)

`Pixbuf`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#signals)Signals

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#area-prepared)`area-prepared`

This signal is emitted when the pixbuf loader has allocated the pixbuf in the desired size.

After this signal is emitted, applications can call
[ PixbufLoaderExt::pixbuf()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PixbufLoaderExt.html#method.pixbuf) to fetch the partially-loaded
pixbuf.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#area-updated)`area-updated`

This signal is emitted when a significant area of the image being loaded has been updated.

Normally it means that a complete scanline has been read in, but it could be a different area as well.

Applications can use this signal to know when to repaint areas of an image that is being loaded.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#closed)`closed`

This signal is emitted when [ PixbufLoaderExt::close()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PixbufLoaderExt.html#method.close) is called.

It can be used by different parts of an application to receive notification when an image loader is closed by the code that drives it.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#size-prepared)`size-prepared`

This signal is emitted when the pixbuf loader has been fed the initial amount of data that is required to figure out the size of the image that it will create.

Applications can call [ PixbufLoaderExt::set_size()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PixbufLoaderExt.html#method.set_size) in response
to this signal to set the desired size to which the image
should be scaled.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

#### pub fn [with_mime_type](https://gtk-rs.org#method.with_mime_type)(mime_type: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[PixbufLoader](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PixbufLoader.html), [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/error/struct.Error.html)>

Creates a new pixbuf loader object that always attempts to parse
image data as if it were an image of MIME type `mime_type`, instead of
identifying the type automatically.

This function is useful if you want an error if the image isn’t the expected MIME type; for loading image formats that can’t be reliably identified by looking at the data; or if the user manually forces a specific MIME type.

The list of supported mime types depends on what image loaders
are installed, but typically “image/png”, “image/jpeg”, “image/gif”,
“image/tiff” and “image/x-xpixmap” are among the supported mime types.
To obtain the full list of supported mime types, call
[ PixbufFormat::mime_types()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PixbufFormat.html#method.mime_types) on each of the

[structs returned by](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PixbufFormat.html)

`PixbufFormat`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html#method.formats)

`Pixbuf::formats()`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#mime_type)`mime_type`

the mime type to be loaded

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-1)Returns

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

#### fn [dynamic_cast](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)<T>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, Self>

Tries to cast to an object of type

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. # InterpType in gdk_pixbuf - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gdk_pixbuf/enum.InterpType.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum InterpType {
    Nearest,
    Tiles,
    Bilinear,
    Hyper,
}
```
## Expand description

Interpolation modes for scaling functions.

The `GDK_INTERP_NEAREST` mode is the fastest scaling method, but has
horrible quality when scaling down; `GDK_INTERP_BILINEAR` is the best
choice if you aren’t sure what to choose, it has a good speed/quality
balance.

**Note**: Cubic filtering is missing from the list; hyperbolic
interpolation is just as fast and results in higher quality.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.Nearest)

### Nearest

Nearest neighbor sampling; this is the fastest and lowest quality mode. Quality is normally unacceptable when scaling down, but may be OK when scaling up.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.Tiles)

### Tiles

This is an accurate simulation of the PostScript image operator without any interpolation enabled. Each pixel is rendered as a tiny parallelogram of solid color, the edges of which are implemented with antialiasing. It resembles nearest neighbor for enlargement, and bilinear for reduction.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.Bilinear)

### Bilinear

Best quality/speed balance; use this mode by default. Bilinear interpolation. For enlargement, it is equivalent to point-sampling the ideal bilinear-interpolated image. For reduction, it is equivalent to laying down small tiles and integrating over the coverage area.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.Hyper)

### Hyper

This is the slowest and highest quality
reconstruction function. It is derived from the hyperbolic filters in
Wolberg’s “Digital Image Warping”, and is formally defined as the
hyperbolic-filter sampling the ideal hyperbolic-filter interpolated
image (the filter is designed to be idempotent for 1:1 pixel mapping).
**Deprecated**: this interpolation filter is deprecated, as in reality
it has a lower quality than the [ Bilinear](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.InterpType.html#variant.Bilinear) filter
(Since: 2.38)

# PixbufAlphaMode in gdk_pixbuf - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gdk_pixbuf/enum.PixbufAlphaMode.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum PixbufAlphaMode {
    Bilevel,
    Full,
}
```
Since 2.42

## Expand description

Control the alpha channel for drawables.

These values can be passed to `gdk_pixbuf_xlib_render_to_drawable_alpha()`
in gdk-pixbuf-xlib to control how the alpha channel of an image should
be handled.

This function can create a bilevel clipping mask (black and white) and use it while painting the image.

In the future, when the X Window System gets an alpha channel extension, it will be possible to do full alpha compositing onto arbitrary drawables. For now both cases fall back to a bilevel clipping mask.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#deprecated-since-242)Deprecated since 2.42

There is no user of GdkPixbufAlphaMode in GdkPixbuf, and the Xlib utility functions have been split out to their own library, gdk-pixbuf-xlib

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.Bilevel)

### Bilevel

Since 2.42

A bilevel clipping mask (black and white) will be created and used to draw the image. Pixels below 0.5 opacity will be considered fully transparent, and all others will be considered fully opaque.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.Full)

### Full

Since 2.42

## Trait Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#trait-implementations)

# PixbufError in gdk_pixbuf - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/gdk_pixbuf/enum.PixbufError.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum PixbufError {
    CorruptImage,
    InsufficientMemory,
    BadOption,
    UnknownType,
    UnsupportedOperation,
    Failed,
    IncompleteAnimation,
}
```
## Expand description

An error code in the `GDK_PIXBUF_ERROR` domain.

Many gdk-pixbuf operations can cause errors in this domain, or in
the `G_FILE_ERROR` domain.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.CorruptImage)

### CorruptImage

An image file was broken somehow.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.InsufficientMemory)

### InsufficientMemory

Not enough memory.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.BadOption)

### BadOption

A bad option was passed to a pixbuf save module.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.UnknownType)

### UnknownType

Unknown image type.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.UnsupportedOperation)

### UnsupportedOperation

Don’t know how to perform the given operation on the type of image at hand.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.Failed)

### Failed

Generic failure code, something went wrong.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.IncompleteAnimation)

### IncompleteAnimation

Only part of the animation was loaded.

Retrieves a static image for the animation.

If an animation is really just a plain image (has only one frame), this function returns that image.

If the animation is an animation, this function returns a reasonable image to use as a static unanimated image, which might be the first frame, or something more sophisticated depending on the file format.

If an animation hasn’t loaded any frames yet, this function will
return `NULL`.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/pixbuf_animation.rs.html#56-76)#### fn [iter](https://gtk-rs.org#method.iter)(&self, start_time: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[SystemTime](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/time/struct.SystemTime.html)>) -> [PixbufAnimationIter](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PixbufAnimationIter.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/pixbuf_animation.rs.html#56-76)

#### fn [iter](https://gtk-rs.org#method.iter)(&self, start_time: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[SystemTime](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/time/struct.SystemTime.html)>) -> [PixbufAnimationIter](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PixbufAnimationIter.html)

Get an iterator for displaying an animation.

The iterator provides the frames that should be displayed at a given time.

`start_time` would normally come from `g_get_current_time()`, and marks
the beginning of animation playback. After creating an iterator, you
should immediately display the pixbuf returned by
[`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::pixbuf()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::pixbuf()]. Then, you should install
a timeout (with `g_timeout_add()`) or by some other mechanism ensure
that you’ll update the image after
[`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::delay_time()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::delay_time()] milliseconds. Each time
the image is updated, you should reinstall the timeout with the new,
possibly-changed delay time.

As a shortcut, if `start_time` is `NULL`, the result of
`g_get_current_time()` will be used automatically.

To update the image (i.e. possibly change the result of
[`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::pixbuf()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::pixbuf()] to a new frame of the animation),
call [`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::advance()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::advance()].

If you’re using [ PixbufLoader](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PixbufLoader.html), in addition to updating the image
after the delay time, you should also update it whenever you
receive the area_updated signal and
[

`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::on_currently_loading_frame()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::on_currently_loading_frame()] returns
`TRUE`. In this case, the frame currently being fed into the loader
has received new data, so needs to be refreshed. The delay time for
a frame may also be modified after an area_updated signal, for
example if the delay time for a frame is encoded in the data after
the frame itself. So your timeout should be reinstalled after any
area_updated signal.A delay time of -1 is possible, indicating “infinite”.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#deprecated-since-244)Deprecated since 2.44

Use a different image loading library for animatable assets

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#start_time)`start_time`

time when the animation starts playing

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns)Returns

an iterator to move over the animation

}## Provided Methods[§](https://gtk-rs.org#provided-methods)

Informs a pixbuf loader that no further writes with
[ write()](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.PixbufLoaderExt.html#method.write) will occur, so that it can free its
internal loading structures.

This function also tries to parse any data that hasn’t yet been parsed; if the remaining data is partial or corrupt, an error will be returned.

If `FALSE` is returned, `error` will be set to an error from the
`GDK_PIXBUF_ERROR` or `G_FILE_ERROR` domains.

If you’re just cancelling a load rather than expecting it to be finished,
passing `NULL` for `error` to ignore it is reasonable.

Remember that this function does not release a reference on the loader, so you will need to explicitly release any reference you hold.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns)Returns

`TRUE` if all image data written so far was successfully
passed out via the update_area signal

Queries the [ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html) that a pixbuf loader is currently creating.

In general it only makes sense to call this function after the
[signal[ Pixbuf](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Pixbuf.html)::area-prepared] signal has been
emitted by the loader; this means that enough data has been read
to know the size of the image that will be allocated.

If the loader has not received enough data via [ write()](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.PixbufLoaderExt.html#method.write),
then this function returns

`NULL`.The returned pixbuf will be the same in all future calls to the loader, so if you want to keep using it, you should acquire a reference to it.

Additionally, if the loader is an animation, it will return the “static
image” of the animation (see [ PixbufAnimationExt::static_image()](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.PixbufAnimationExt.html#method.static_image)).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-3)Returns

size of the image by calling [ set_size()](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.PixbufLoaderExt.html#method.set_size) from a
signal handler for the ::size-prepared signal.

Attempts to set the desired image size are ignored after the emission of the ::size-prepared signal.

#### fn [delay_time](https://gtk-rs.org#method.delay_time)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)>

Time in milliseconds, returning `None` implies showing the same pixbuf forever.
Gets the number of milliseconds the current pixbuf should be displayed,
or -1 if the current pixbuf should be displayed forever.

The `g_timeout_add()` function conveniently takes a timeout in milliseconds,
so you can use a timeout to schedule the next update.

Note that some formats, like GIF, might clamp the timeout values in the image file to avoid updates that are just too quick. The minimum timeout for GIF images is currently 20 milliseconds.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#deprecated-since-244)Deprecated since 2.44

Use a different image loading library for animatable assets

delay time in milliseconds (thousandths of a second)

Gets the current pixbuf which should be displayed.

The pixbuf might not be the same size as the animation itself
([ PixbufAnimationExt::width()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PixbufAnimationExt.html#method.width),

[).](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PixbufAnimationExt.html#method.height)

`PixbufAnimationExt::height()`This pixbuf should be displayed for [`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::delay_time()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::delay_time()]
milliseconds.

The caller of this function does not own a reference to the returned
pixbuf; the returned pixbuf will become invalid when the iterator
advances to the next frame, which may happen anytime you call
[`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::advance()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::advance()].

Copy the pixbuf to keep it (don’t just add a reference), as it may get recycled as you advance the iterator.

#### fn [on_currently_loading_frame](https://gtk-rs.org#method.on_currently_loading_frame)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Used to determine how to respond to the area_updated signal on
[ PixbufLoader](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PixbufLoader.html) when loading an animation.

The `::area_updated` signal is emitted for an area of the frame currently
streaming in to the loader. So if you’re on the currently loading frame,
you will need to redraw the screen for the updated area.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/subclass/pixbuf_animation_iter.rs.html#118-120)#### fn [advance](https://gtk-rs.org#method.advance)(&self, current_time: [SystemTime](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/time/struct.SystemTime.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gdk_pixbuf/subclass/pixbuf_animation_iter.rs.html#118-120)

#### fn [advance](https://gtk-rs.org#method.advance)(&self, current_time: [SystemTime](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/time/struct.SystemTime.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Possibly advances an animation to a new frame.

Chooses the frame based on the start time passed to
[ PixbufAnimationExtManual::iter()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PixbufAnimationExtManual.html#method.iter).

`current_time` would normally come from `g_get_current_time()`, and
must be greater than or equal to the time passed to
[ PixbufAnimationExtManual::iter()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PixbufAnimationExtManual.html#method.iter), and must increase or remain
unchanged each time [

`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::pixbuf()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::pixbuf()] is
called. That is, you can’t go backward in time; animations only
play forward.As a shortcut, pass `NULL` for the current time and `g_get_current_time()`
will be invoked on your behalf. So you only need to explicitly pass
`current_time` if you’re doing something odd like playing the animation
at double speed.

If this function returns `FALSE`, there’s no need to update the animation
display, assuming the display had been rendered prior to advancing;
if `TRUE`, you need to call [`PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::pixbuf()`][crate::prelude::PixbufAnimationIterExtManual::pixbuf()]
and update the display with the new pixbuf.

Use a different image loading library for animatable assets

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#current_time)`current_time`

current time

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-3)Returns

`TRUE` if the image may need updating

This virtual function is always invoked in the local instance. It
gets passed a pointer to a [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)-terminated copy of @argv and is
expected to remove arguments that it handled (shifting up remaining
arguments).

The last argument to local_command_line() is a pointer to the @status variable which can used to set the exit status that is returned from g_application_run().

See g_application_run() for more details on #GApplication startup.

Opens the given files.

In essence, this results in the #GApplication::open signal being emitted in the primary instance.

@n_files must be greater than zero.

@hint is simply passed through to the ::open signal. It is intended to be used by applications that have multiple modes for opening files (eg: “view” vs “edit”, etc). Unless you have a need for this functionality, you should use “”.

The application must be registered before calling this function
and it must have the [ ApplicationFlags::HANDLES_OPEN](https://gtk-rs.org/gio/auto/flags/struct.ApplicationFlags.html#associatedconstant.HANDLES_OPEN) flag set.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/subclass/boxed.rs.html#37)#### const [ALLOW_NAME_CONFLICT](https://gtk-rs.org#associatedconstant.ALLOW_NAME_CONFLICT): [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) = false

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/subclass/boxed.rs.html#37)

#### const [ALLOW_NAME_CONFLICT](https://gtk-rs.org#associatedconstant.ALLOW_NAME_CONFLICT): [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) = false

Allow name conflicts for this boxed type.

By default, trying to register a type with a name that was registered before will panic. If
this is set to `true` then a new name will be selected by appending a counter.

This is useful for defining new types in Rust library crates that might be linked multiple times in the same process.

A consequence of setting this to `true` is that it’s not guaranteed that
`glib::Type::from_name(Self::NAME).unwrap() == Self::static_type()`.

Optional.

# ClassStruct in gdk_pixbuf::subclass::prelude - Rust

`pub unsafe trait ClassStruct: `[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) + 'static {

    fn [class_init](https://gtk-rs.org#method.class_init)(&mut self) { ... }
}## Expand description

Trait implemented by structs that implement a `GObject` C class struct.

The struct must be `#[repr(C)]` and have the parent type’s class struct
as the first field.

See [ basic::ClassStruct](https://gtk-rs.org/basic/struct.ClassStruct.html) for a basic implementation of this that can
be used most of the time and should only not be used if additional fields are
required in the class struct, e.g. for declaring new virtual methods.
